claims.claim: The study retrieved 843 WoSCC candidates on 6 January 2024 and included 652 English articles and reviews from 2017–2023 after title and abstract screening.
The corpus contains 168 sources, 2,654 authors, and 19,174 references, with 149.8% annual growth and 13.29 average citations per document.
Document composition was 619 articles, 4 data papers, 13 proceedings papers, and 16 reviews.
Annual publications were 1, 1, 16, 48, 113, 230, and 243 from 2017 through 2023.
China produced 426 papers and the United States 142.
China and the United States led output and collaboration, while worldwide cooperation needs strengthening.
The leading institutions listed were all Chinese, led by the Chinese Academy of Sciences with 39 publications.
Briefings in Bioinformatics led publication count with 75, while Bioinformatics led total citations with 1,580.
You Zhu-Hong led authors with 11 publications and the listed top authors were Chinese.
The leading cited papers and their global and local citation counts are those reported in Table 7.
GNN applications primarily concern drug-target interaction, drug repurposing, and drug-drug interaction, with graph convolutional methods central.
Data availability, ethics, computing resources, and interpretability are key technical challenges.
Bibliometrix, VOSviewer, CiteSpace, and Excel were used for performance, collaboration, cocitation, keyword, discipline, and burst analyses.
Citation thresholds directly measure paper quality.
The report provides extensive performance, collaboration, journal, author, citation, keyword, and trend coverage but limited explicit inferential caution.
The corpus contains 456 unique works from 2018–2023, acquired exhaustively and deduplicated.
The stated metadata completeness percentages are correct.
Annual output rose from 1 to 190 and endpoint CAGR was 185.6%.
Briefings in Bioinformatics, Thin Nguyen, and the Chinese Academy of Sciences lead productivity.
Bradford Zone 1 has 5 sources and 148 documents.
Mean citations are 59.82, median 24.00, maximum 1,210, and 22 works are uncited.
GraphDTA and Attentive FP are the two most-cited included works.
The six network sizes, displayed structures, and principal nodes are as reported.
Institutional collaboration is largely nationally bounded.
The cocitation base is anchored by seminal GNN and molecular-featurization works.
Four coupling communities definitively correspond to molecular representation, DTI, biological network analysis, and surveys.
The field is hyper-exponential, method-core/application-periphery, and diversifying toward geometry, self-supervision, and interpretability.
The report covers acquisition, quality, performance, social, conceptual, intellectual, and limitations dimensions.

rationale: A is more comprehensive for its paired evidence, especially on countries, institutions, journals, authors, document composition, citation structure, and keyword findings. B is better organized and caveated, but substantial portions of its intellectual, geographic, and future-facing synthesis go beyond the canonical network and abstract evidence.

claims.claim: The study screened 231 records, retained 220 after document-type exclusions, and included 219 English publications from 2015–2022.
The final corpus comprised 164 articles and 55 reviews after the non-English review was removed.
Publication volume fluctuated but generally increased, especially after 2019.
China, the United States, and Germany were leading contributors.
China led total citations and H-index, while South Korea led average citations.
A fitted curve projected approximately 300 annual articles by 2050.
That projection establishes the field's future output.
Wang Y. and Zhang H. led author output with six publications each.
There were 141 core authors and cooperation maps covered authors, countries, and institutions.
Citation-burst analysis identified Valadi H as strongest, followed by Thery, Raposo, Kowal, and Li.
There were 317 recurring keywords and seven named keyword clusters.
Expression, cells, Cas9, and RNA were the most frequent listed keywords.
Gene therapy and nanovesicles were enduring concepts, while genome, protein delivery, and plasma were emerging.
This was the first bibliometric study of the topic.
Citation frequency reflects publication quality or author research value.
The report supplies broad country, author, institution, citation-burst, journal, and keyword coverage but limited methodological caution.
The corpus contains 259 unique publications from 2015–2022, retrieved exhaustively and exactly deduplicated.
The stated metadata completeness values are correct.
Output rose from 2 in 2015 to 72 in 2022 and endpoint CAGR was 66.85%.
The growth series has emergence, acceleration, and consolidation phases.
All source-labelled articles prove that the corpus contains no reviews and is dominated by primary research.
Mean citations are 72.09, median 32.00, maximum 1,436, and 35 works are uncited.
The leading cited works and their counts concern Pseudomonas, RNA EV delivery, hybrid EV–liposome CRISPR delivery, and related delivery topics.
Those cited works prove that EV–CRISPR delivery dominates the impact landscape.
Xiaohui Chen leads author output; Harvard, Peking, and Sun Yat-sen tie for institutions; International Journal of Molecular Sciences leads sources.
Bradford and all five network sizes, clusters, and top mapped nodes are as reported.
The overlay establishes a shift from foundational EV work to newer applied therapeutic themes.
The field is rapidly maturing toward clinical relevance and will next move into preclinical and clinical translation.
Eleven of the top fifteen institutions are Chinese.
The report acknowledges source, citation-window, parameterization, abstract-only, keyword, and final-year limitations.

rationale: A has unique and extensive country, author, burst, journal, and keyword-evolution coverage, while B is more reproducible and explicitly caveated but overinterprets maps and source-level document labels. Their complementary strengths and material inferential weaknesses are closely balanced.
